0.0.n: ということ indicates the situation just discussed; the full phrase introduces a transition.

0.1.n: こと turns the preceding idea into something the speaker can refer to.

0.2.n: で completes ということで, linking the previous discussion to what comes next.

0.3.n: 私 is a neutral, polite way to refer to yourself.

0.4.n: は marks 私 as the topic of the conversation.

0.5.n: まず introduces the first thing the speaker wants to discuss.

0.7.n: 今回 specifies this particular shopping occasion.

0.8.n: 購入した is the plain past form of 購入する and describes what was bought.

0.9.n: の turns 今回購入した into a noun phrase referring to the things purchased.

0.10.n: は introduces the purchased items as a topic, with their identities coming later.

1.0.n: ここ points to a place near the speaker.

1.1.n: に marks the location where the boxes are arranged.

1.2.n: ね gently draws the listener's attention to the location.

1.4.n: ちょっと casually downplays the quantity here rather than giving an exact count.

1.5.n: 箱 can refer to one box or several; the scene makes it plural here.

1.6.n: が identifies the boxes as what is lined up.

1.7.n: 並んでる is casual 並んでいる, describing the resulting arrangement rather than an ongoing action.

1.8.n: ん is shortened の; it presents the visible arrangement as background for the explanation.

1.9.n: です adds politeness to the explanation ending in ん.

1.10.n: けれども softly connects to what follows, without expressing a strong contrast here.

2.0.n: 3 combines with 月 to name March.

2.1.n: 月 follows a number to specify a calendar month.

2.2.n: 25日 names the day of the month, not a duration here.

2.3.n: に marks the date of release.

2.4.n: 発売 refers to putting a product on sale.

2.5.n: を connects 発売 to した; 発売をする is an expanded version of 発売する.

2.6.n: した is the plain past of する; 発売をした describes the product's release here.

2.7.n: この points to the nearby iPad and must come before a noun.

2.9.n: 最新 describes the newest available version of the product.

2.10.n: の connects 最新 to the product it describes.

2.11.n: iPad is Apple's tablet product name, used here as part of iPad Pro.

2.13.n: Pro is the model designation within the product name iPad Pro.

2.14.n: と links this purchase to the next item in the list.

3.0.n: あと introduces another item after the one already mentioned.

3.1.n: は combines with あと to shift attention to the next purchase.

3.3.n: 本当に emphasizes how recently the keyboard was released.

3.4.n: 先日 refers to a recent day without specifying the exact date.

3.5.n: 発売された is the plain past passive of 発売する, focusing on the product rather than whoever released it.

3.6.n: ばかり after a past verb indicates that the event happened very recently.

3.7.n: の lets 発売されたばかり describe the following product.

3.8.n: こちら politely points to the item near the speaker.

3.9.n: の connects こちら to Magic Keyboard, identifying the item being shown.

3.10.n: Magic is part of Apple's product name Magic Keyboard, not a separate description here.

3.12.n: Keyboard completes the product name Magic Keyboard.

3.13.n: と continues the list, indicating that another purchase follows.

4.0.n: あと introduces the final additional item.

4.1.n: は marks the shift to the remaining purchase in あとは.

4.3.n: この identifies the nearby Apple Pencil and directly precedes its name.

4.4.n: Apple is the company name and part of the product name Apple Pencil.

4.6.n: Pencil completes Apple Pencil, the name of Apple's stylus.

4.7.n: の connects the full list of products to its total count, ３点.

4.8.n: 点 is a counting word used for individual items or products.

4.9.n: を marks the three items as what the speaker purchased.

4.10.n: 購入しました is the polite past form of 購入する.

0.lit: So, as for me, first, as for what I purchased this time…
0.tip: A plain verb followed by のは introduces what someone did as a topic: what I purchased is…

1.lit: Here, you see, a few boxes are lined up, but…
1.tip: 並んでる shortens 並んでいる and describes boxes already arranged in a row.

2.lit: This latest iPad Pro that had its release on March 25th, and…
2.tip: Japanese puts the release information before the product name, where English would use a following that clause.

3.lit: Also, this Magic Keyboard that really was just released the other day, and…
3.tip: A past verb plus ばかり means the event has only recently happened.

4.lit: Also, this Apple Pencil: I purchased the three items.
4.tip: の３点 sums up all three listed products, not three Apple Pencils.
